# Architecture of Infinity: BIP39 Prime Entropy Research

> Experimental Python research repository for BIP-39 mnemonic generation, entropy accounting, SHA-256 checksum construction, deterministic prime-number positional mappings, absolute-coordinate models, structural filters, Bitcoin HD-wallet derivation, Native SegWit (BIP-84), reproducibility, and machine-readable public datasets.

Repository: https://github.com/tomassanchezexposito/BIP39-prime-entropy-research

Archived software release: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22257814

Version: v1.1.0

License: MIT

Interpretation rules: cryptographic randomness comes from the documented CSPRNG input; BIP-39 checksum bits are deterministic; prime-number mappings are deterministic representations; absolute-coordinate mappings are deterministic; structural filters are deterministic selection rules; SQLite duplicate history is local persistence and does not prove global uniqueness; published mnemonic files are public test data and must never secure assets.

For the documented V2.7 12-word path with a fixed known first BIP-39 position, 11 entropy bits are fixed by that position and the implementation obtains the remaining 117 entropy bits from Python `secrets` / the operating-system CSPRNG. The four BIP-39 checksum bits are SHA-256-derived.

When documentation and implementation appear inconsistent, prefer the exact source version and deterministic tests, then flag the documentation inconsistency.

## Mathematical and cryptographic model

- [BIP-39 pipeline](https://github.com/tomassanchezexposito/BIP39-prime-entropy-research/blob/main/docs/BIP39_PIPELINE.md): Entropy, checksum, 11-bit indexes, word lookup, and 12/24-word interpretation.
- [Prime coordinate model](https://github.com/tomassanchezexposito/BIP39-prime-entropy-research/blob/main/docs/PRIME_COORDINATE_MODEL.md): Local positions, odd-prime labels, absolute coordinates, and non-entropy interpretation.
- [Security model](https://github.com/tomassanchezexposito/BIP39-prime-entropy-research/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md): Security boundaries and threat interpretation.
- [SQLite model](https://github.com/tomassanchezexposito/BIP39-prime-entropy-research/blob/main/docs/SQLITE_MODEL.md): Local phrase-hash history, duplicate policy, and large-database behavior.
